3-5.title: The School Rooftop Weather Station
3-5.titleEs: La estación meteorológica en el techo de la escuela

scene.heading: Fourth-Grade Weather Log: Monday to Wednesday
scene.headingEs: Registro del tiempo de cuarto grado: lunes a miércoles
facts: Monday: Clear sky, wind speed 4 miles per hour, 0 inches of rain in the rain gauge.
Lunes: Cielo despejado, viento de 4 millas por hora, 0 pulgadas de lluvia en el pluviómetro.
Tuesday: Dark gray cumulonimbus clouds arrived, wind speed rose to 18 miles per hour.
Martes: Llegaron nubes cumulonimbos grises oscuras, el viento subió a 18 millas por hora.
Wednesday morning: The rain gauge measured 2 inches of rainfall and puddles covered the field.
Miércoles por la mañana: El pluviómetro midió 2 pulgadas de lluvia y los charcos cubrieron la cancha.
scene.teacherPrompt: Look at the fourth-grade weather log from Monday to Wednesday. We are going to describe what changed in the sky and explain how the weather tools helped the class measure the storm. First, listen to Maya.

modelStudent.name: Maya
modelStudent.text: On Monday the sky was clear and the rain gauge had zero inches of water. By Wednesday morning, the rain gauge collected two inches of rainfall because a storm arrived on Tuesday.

check.q: What did Maya include to make her spoken explanation clear?

options.text: She named exact measurements from Monday and Wednesday and connected them with 'because'.
She guessed what the weather would be next month without looking at the chart.
She only named her favorite season of the year.

check.why: Maya used specific numbers from the weather log and explained the cause with 'because'.

turn1.prompt: Turn 1 (Tier A · Describe): What did the students observe on Monday compared with Tuesday?
turn1.promptEs: Turno 1 (Nivel A · Describir): ¿Qué observaron los estudiantes el lunes en comparación con el martes?

parts.answer: clear with light wind,

options: dark clouds arrived and wind speed rose to 18 miles per hour.
the rain gauge broke in half.
parts.answer: dark clouds arrived and wind speed rose to 18 miles per hour.

turn1.model: On Monday the sky was clear with light wind, whereas on Tuesday dark clouds arrived and wind speed rose to 18 miles per hour.

turn2.prompt: Turn 2 (Tier B · Explain): How did the rain gauge show the effect of Tuesday's storm on Wednesday morning?
turn2.promptEs: Turno 2 (Nivel B · Explicar): ¿Cómo mostró el pluviómetro el efecto de la tormenta del martes el miércoles por la mañana?
parts: Because the dark storm clouds brought heavy rain on Tuesday night,

options: the rain gauge measured 2 inches of rainfall
parts.answer: the rain gauge measured 2 inches of rainfall
on Wednesday morning.

turn2.model: Because the dark storm clouds brought heavy rain on Tuesday night, the rain gauge measured 2 inches of rainfall on Wednesday morning.

turn3.prompt: Turn 3 (Tier C · Extended Speaking): Explain to a younger student how watching clouds and wind speed helps scientists prepare for rain. Use at least one target word and one connector.
turn3.promptEs: Turno 3 (Nivel C · Expresión oral extendida): Explícale a un estudiante menor cómo observar las nubes y el viento ayuda a los científicos a prepararse para la lluvia. Usa al menos una palabra clave y un conector.
frames: When scientists observe dark clouds and stronger wind, they know ___ because ___.
Tracking wind speed and checking the rain gauge helps us ___ so ___.
turn3.model: When scientists observe dark clouds and rising wind speed, they can warn the community because heavy rainfall will soon fill the rain gauge.

familyTalk.en: Talk at home: How do we decide what to wear or carry in the morning when we look at the sky?
familyTalk.es: Hablen en casa: ¿Cómo decidimos qué ropa ponernos o si llevar paraguas por la mañana cuando miramos el cielo?

teacherTip.en: Have partners take turns playing the Teacher and the Student using Turns 1, 2, and 3 before recording independently.
teacherTip.es: Pida a las parejas que se turnen para hacer de docente y estudiante usando los Turnos 1, 2 y 3 antes de grabar de forma independiente.

3-5.title: Goods and Services at the Farmers Market
3-5.titleEs: Bienes y servicios en el mercado agrícola

scene.heading: Saturday Community Market Map
scene.headingEs: Mapa del mercado comunitario del sábado
facts: Booth A (Orchard Farm): Sells baskets of fresh apples, peaches, and honey jars (Goods).
Puesto A (Granja del Huerto): Vende canastas de manzanas frescas, duraznos y frascos de miel (Bienes).
Booth B (Bike Repair Corner): Fixes flat tires and adjusts bicycle brakes for riders (Services).
Puesto B (Rincón de reparación de bicicletas): Repara llantas ponchadas y ajusta los frenos (Servicios).
Community Exchange: Families use money to buy food from farmers and pay mechanics for repair work.
Intercambio comunitario: Las familias compran alimentos a los agricultores y pagan a los mecánicos por su trabajo.
scene.teacherPrompt: Look at the Saturday Community Market Map. Some workers sell goods you can hold, while other workers provide services that help people. Listen to Leo explain Booth A.

modelStudent.name: Leo
modelStudent.text: At Booth A, the farmer sells fresh apples and jars of honey. Those are goods because customers can touch them and carry them home in a basket.

check.q: Why did Leo say apples and honey are goods?

options.text: Because customers can touch them and take them home.
Because a mechanic repairs them with a wrench.
Because they are free for everyone on Mondays.

check.why: Goods are physical items people grow or make that buyers can touch and take home.

turn1.prompt: Turn 1 (Tier A · Describe): What happens at Booth B, the Bike Repair Corner?
turn1.promptEs: Turno 1 (Nivel A · Describir): ¿Qué ocurre en el Puesto B, el rincón de reparación de bicicletas?
parts: At Booth B, the bike mechanic

options: fixes flat tires and adjusts brakes
parts.answer: fixes flat tires and adjusts brakes
for riders in the community.

turn1.model: At Booth B, the bike mechanic fixes flat tires and adjusts brakes for riders in the community.

turn2.prompt: Turn 2 (Tier B · Compare): How is Booth B different from Booth A?
turn2.promptEs: Turno 2 (Nivel B · Comparar): ¿En qué se diferencia el Puesto B del Puesto A?
parts: Booth A sells physical goods like apples,

options: whereas Booth B provides a helpful service
and Booth B also sells apples
parts.answer: whereas Booth B provides a helpful service
by repairing bicycles for neighbors.

turn2.model: Booth A sells physical goods like apples, whereas Booth B provides a helpful service by repairing bicycles for neighbors.

turn3.prompt: Turn 3 (Tier C · Extended Speaking): Explain why a neighborhood needs both goods and services every week. Use at least one target word and one connector.
turn3.promptEs: Turno 3 (Nivel C · Expresión oral extendida): Explica por qué un vecindario necesita tanto bienes como servicios cada semana. Usa al menos una palabra clave y un conector.
frames: A community needs both goods and services because ___ while ___.
At the market, families buy goods such as ___, and they also use services so ___.
turn3.model: A community needs both goods and services because families buy goods like fresh food to eat, while workers provide services that keep bikes and homes working safely.

familyTalk.en: Talk at home: What is one good our family bought this week, and what is one service someone in our community provides?
familyTalk.es: Hablen en casa: ¿Cuál es un bien que compró nuestra familia esta semana y cuál es un servicio que presta alguien de nuestra comunidad?

teacherTip.en: Prompt students to stress the contrast connector 'whereas' or 'while' when comparing goods and services aloud.
teacherTip.es: Anime a los estudiantes a enfatizar el conector de contraste 'whereas' o 'while' al comparar bienes y servicios en voz alta.

3-5.title: Comparing Garden Plots by Area and Perimeter
3-5.titleEs: Comparación de parcelas de jardín por área y perímetro

scene.heading: Two Rectangular Plans for the Class Vegetable Bed
scene.headingEs: Dos planos rectangulares para la huerta de la clase
facts: Plot A measures 4 feet wide by 4 feet long: Area = 16 square feet, Perimeter = 16 feet of wooden border.
La Parcela A mide 4 pies de ancho por 4 pies de largo: Área = 16 pies cuadrados, Perímetro = 16 pies de borde.
Plot B measures 2 feet wide by 8 feet long: Area = 16 square feet, Perimeter = 20 feet of wooden border.
La Parcela B mide 2 pies de ancho por 8 pies de largo: Área = 16 pies cuadrados, Perímetro = 20 pies de borde.
Garden rule: Each tomato plant needs 1 square foot of soil inside the plot, and wooden boards go around the outside edge.
Regla del jardín: Cada planta necesita 1 pie cuadrado de tierra adentro, y las tablas de madera van alrededor del borde exterior.
scene.teacherPrompt: Look at Plot A and Plot B for the class vegetable garden. Both plots hold the same number of plants inside, but they need different amounts of wood around the outside. Listen to Maya.

modelStudent.name: Maya
modelStudent.text: Plot A and Plot B both have an area of 16 square feet inside, so both plots can hold 16 tomato plants.

check.q: Why can both Plot A and Plot B hold the exact same number of tomato plants?

options.text: Because both rectangles have an area of 16 square feet.
Because both rectangles have the exact same perimeter.
Because Plot B has no wooden border at all.

check.why: The space inside a shape is its area, and both plots have an area of 16 square feet.

turn1.prompt: Turn 1 (Tier A · Describe): What are the length, width, and perimeter of Plot B?
turn1.promptEs: Turno 1 (Nivel A · Describir): ¿Cuáles son el largo, el ancho y el perímetro de la Parcela B?

parts.answer: 2 feet wide and 8 feet long,

parts: and its perimeter around the outside is

parts.answer: 20 feet.

turn1.model: Plot B is 2 feet wide and 8 feet long, and its perimeter around the outside is 20 feet.

turn2.prompt: Turn 2 (Tier B · Explain): If the class only has 16 feet of wooden boards for the outside border, which plot should they build and why?
turn2.promptEs: Turno 2 (Nivel B · Explicar): Si la clase solo tiene 16 pies de tablas de madera para el borde exterior, ¿qué parcela deben construir y por qué?
parts: The class should build Plot A

parts.answer: because its perimeter is 16 feet,
20 feet of wooden border.

turn2.model: The class should build Plot A because its perimeter is 16 feet, whereas Plot B requires 20 feet of wooden border.

turn3.prompt: Turn 3 (Tier C · Extended Speaking): Explain in your own words how two rectangles can have the same area but different perimeters. Use at least one math word and one connector.
turn3.promptEs: Turno 3 (Nivel C · Expresión oral extendida): Explica con tus propias palabras cómo dos rectángulos pueden tener la misma área pero diferente perímetro. Usa al menos una palabra matemática y un conector.
frames: Although Plot A and Plot B have the same area of 16 square feet, their perimeters are different because ___.
Area measures the square feet inside a shape, while perimeter measures ___.
turn3.model: Although both plots have an area of 16 square feet inside, Plot B has a longer perimeter because its skinny shape stretches out the outside edge to 20 feet.

familyTalk.en: Talk at home: Where do we measure around the outside edge (perimeter) vs. covering the inside space (area) in our home?
familyTalk.es: Hablen en casa: ¿Dónde medimos alrededor del borde exterior (perímetro) en comparación con cubrir el espacio interior (área) en nuestra casa?

teacherTip.en: Have students trace the inside squares with an open palm when saying 'area' and trace the outside frame with one finger when saying 'perimeter'.
teacherTip.es: Pida a los estudiantes que recorran los cuadrados interiores con la palma al decir 'area' y el borde exterior con un dedo al decir 'perimeter'.

3-5.title: Retelling How a Character Solves a Problem
3-5.titleEs: Relatar cómo un personaje resuelve un problema

scene.heading: Story Storyboard: The Lantern Parade
scene.headingEs: Guion gráfico del cuento: El desfile de los faroles
facts: Beginning: Mateo spent all afternoon folding a paper star lantern for the evening neighborhood parade.
Inicio: Mateo pasó toda la tarde doblando un farol de papel en forma de estrella para el desfile nocturno.
Middle (Problem): A sudden gust of wind tore one paper wing right before the parade lined up.
Medio (Problema): Una ráfaga repentina de viento rompió un ala de papel justo antes de que empezara el desfile.
End (Solution): Mateo's cousin Lucia shared her gold ribbon so they could tape and tie the wing stronger than before.
Final (Solución): Su prima Lucía compartió su cinta dorada para sujetar el ala y dejarla más firme que antes.
scene.teacherPrompt: Look at the three parts of the story 'The Lantern Parade.' When we retell a story aloud, we tell the beginning, the problem in the middle, and how the characters solved it at the end. Listen to Leo.

modelStudent.name: Leo
modelStudent.text: At the beginning of the story, Mateo folded a paper star lantern so he could carry it in the evening neighborhood parade.

check.q: What transition phrase did Leo use to start his story retell?

options.text: He started with 'At the beginning of the story' and named who and what.
He started with the ending first and skipped Mateo's name.
He only listed three random words.

check.why: Clear story retells use time-order transitions and name the character and action.

turn1.prompt: Turn 1 (Tier A · Describe): What problem happened in the middle of the story?
turn1.promptEs: Turno 1 (Nivel A · Describir): ¿Qué problema ocurrió a la mitad del cuento?
parts: In the middle of the story,

options: a sudden gust of wind tore one paper wing
Mateo forgot where the park was
parts.answer: a sudden gust of wind tore one paper wing

options: right before the parade lined up.
parts.answer: right before the parade lined up.

turn1.model: In the middle of the story, a sudden gust of wind tore one paper wing right before the parade lined up.

turn2.prompt: Turn 2 (Tier B · Sequence & Solution): How did Mateo and Lucia solve the problem at the end?
turn2.promptEs: Turno 2 (Nivel B · Secuencia y solución): ¿Cómo resolvieron el problema Mateo y Lucía al final?
parts: Finally, Lucia shared her gold ribbon

options: so they could tie the torn wing
because she wanted to go home
and they threw the lantern away
parts.answer: so they could tie the torn wing

options: make the lantern stronger than before.
parts.answer: make the lantern stronger than before.

turn2.model: Finally, Lucia shared her gold ribbon so they could tie the torn wing and make the lantern stronger than before.

turn3.prompt: Turn 3 (Tier C · Extended Speaking): Retell the whole story from beginning to end in two or three connected sentences, and tell what lesson Mateo learned. Use at least one target word and one connector.
turn3.promptEs: Turno 3 (Nivel C · Expresión oral extendida): Vuelve a contar todo el cuento de principio a fin en dos o tres oraciones conectadas, y di qué lección aprendió Mateo. Usa al menos una palabra clave y un conector.
frames: Mateo made a paper lantern for the parade, but when the wind tore it, Lucia shared her ribbon so ___.
When the wind damaged Mateo's lantern, he learned that teamwork matters because ___.
turn3.model: Mateo folded a paper lantern for the parade, and when the wind tore one wing, Lucia shared her gold ribbon so they could fix it together.

familyTalk.en: Talk at home: Tell a story about a time when something broke or went wrong and two people in our family worked together to fix it.
familyTalk.es: Hablen en casa: Cuenten una historia sobre una vez en que algo salió mal y dos personas de la familia trabajaron juntas para solucionarlo.

teacherTip.en: Display the three sequence anchors (At the beginning -> Then, when -> Finally, so) on the board for oral retells across any fiction text.
teacherTip.es: Muestre los tres conectores de secuencia (At the beginning -> Then, when -> Finally, so) en la pizarra para relatos orales.

6-8.title: Urban Heat Islands and Tree Canopy Data
6-8.titleEs: Islas de calor urbano y datos de cobertura arbórea

scene.heading: City Neighborhood Summer Temperature Study (3:00 PM)
scene.headingEs: Estudio de temperatura de verano en tres barrios (3:00 p. m.)
facts: Oakwood District: 45 percent tree canopy cover, dark asphalt cover 20 percent, average surface temperature 82 degrees Fahrenheit.
Distrito Oakwood: 45 por ciento de cobertura de árboles, 20 por ciento de asfalto oscuro, temperatura superficial media de 82 grados.
Midtown Plaza: 22 percent tree canopy cover, dark asphalt cover 48 percent, average surface temperature 91 degrees Fahrenheit.
Midtown Plaza: 22 por ciento de cobertura de árboles, 48 por ciento de asfalto oscuro, temperatura superficial media de 91 grados.
Harbor Industrial: 6 percent tree canopy cover, dark asphalt cover 75 percent, average surface temperature 99 degrees Fahrenheit.
Harbor Industrial: 6 por ciento de cobertura de árboles, 75 por ciento de asfalto oscuro, temperatura superficial media de 99 grados.
scene.teacherPrompt: Examine the summer temperature study across three city neighborhoods. Scientists call areas with lots of dark pavement and few trees 'urban heat islands.' Listen to Maya analyze the pattern.

modelStudent.name: Maya
modelStudent.text: The data shows a clear inverse pattern: as tree canopy cover decreases from 45 percent in Oakwood to 6 percent in Harbor Industrial, average surface temperature rises from 82 degrees to 99 degrees.

check.q: What makes Maya's opening statement strong on a WIDA speaking task?

options.text: She names the overall trend and backs it up by comparing specific numbers from two neighborhoods.
She says it is hot in the summer without mentioning any neighborhood or number.
She reads the column headers without forming a complete sentence.

check.why: Strong academic speaking states the pattern clearly and cites exact data points as evidence.

turn1.prompt: Turn 1 (Tier A · Describe Data): Compare the tree canopy cover and surface temperature of Midtown Plaza and Harbor Industrial.
turn1.promptEs: Turno 1 (Nivel A · Describir datos): Compara la cobertura de árboles y la temperatura de Midtown Plaza y Harbor Industrial.
parts: Midtown Plaza has 22 percent tree canopy and a temperature of 91 degrees,

options: whereas Harbor Industrial has only 6 percent tree canopy
and Harbor Industrial has 90 percent trees
parts.answer: whereas Harbor Industrial has only 6 percent tree canopy
99 degrees Fahrenheit.

turn1.model: Midtown Plaza has 22 percent tree canopy and a temperature of 91 degrees, whereas Harbor Industrial has only 6 percent tree canopy and reaches 99 degrees Fahrenheit.

turn2.prompt: Turn 2 (Tier B · Explain Mechanism): Why does Harbor Industrial reach a much higher afternoon temperature than Oakwood District?
turn2.promptEs: Turno 2 (Nivel B · Explicar el mecanismo): ¿Por qué Harbor Industrial alcanza una temperatura mucho más alta por la tarde que Oakwood District?

options: because 75 percent of its surface is dark asphalt that absorbs solar energy,
because it is closer to the North Pole,
since trees make the pavement hotter,
parts.answer: because 75 percent of its surface is dark asphalt that absorbs solar energy,

options: 45 percent tree canopy provides shade and cools the air.
parts.answer: 45 percent tree canopy provides shade and cools the air.

turn2.model: Harbor Industrial reaches 99 degrees because 75 percent of its surface is dark asphalt that absorbs solar energy, while Oakwood's 45 percent tree canopy provides shade and cools the air.

turn3.prompt: Turn 3 (Tier C · Argue from Evidence): The city council has funds to plant 500 new street trees in one district. Argue which district should receive the trees first, citing data from the study.
turn3.promptEs: Turno 3 (Nivel C · Argumentar con evidencia): El concejo municipal tiene fondos para plantar 500 árboles nuevos en un distrito. Argumenta qué distrito debe recibirlos primero, citando datos del estudio.
frames: The city council should plant the 500 trees in Harbor Industrial first because ___, whereas Oakwood ___.
Since Harbor Industrial has 75 percent dark asphalt and only 6 percent tree canopy, planting trees there will ___ therefore ___.
turn3.model: The city council should plant the 500 trees in Harbor Industrial first because it has only 6 percent tree canopy and 75 percent dark asphalt, whereas Oakwood already has shade that keeps its temperature 17 degrees cooler.

familyTalk.en: Talk at home: Which streets or parks in our city feel cooler on a hot summer afternoon, and what makes the difference?
familyTalk.es: Hablen en casa: ¿Qué calles o parques de nuestra ciudad se sienten más frescos en una tarde calurosa de verano y qué marca la diferencia?

teacherTip.en: Encourage students to pair a causal connector ('because' / 'since') with a contrast connector ('whereas' / 'while') in Turn 3 to hit bridging-level sentence complexity.
teacherTip.es: Anime a los estudiantes a combinar un conector causal ('because' / 'since') con uno de contraste ('whereas' / 'while') en el Turno 3.

6-8.title: River Valley Civilizations and Trade Networks
6-8.titleEs: Civilizaciones de valles fluviales y redes comerciales

scene.heading: Archaeological Map: Why Early Cities Grew Along Major Rivers
scene.headingEs: Mapa arqueológico: Por qué las primeras ciudades crecieron junto a grandes ríos
facts: Seasonal Flooding & Silt: Annual river floods deposited nutrient-rich silt across the floodplain.
Inundaciones estacionales y limo: Las crecidas anuales depositaban limo rico en nutrientes en la llanura.
Irrigation Canals: Farmers dug canals and basins to channel river water to barley and wheat fields during dry months.
Canales de riego: Los agricultores cavaron canales para llevar agua del río a los cultivos durante los meses secos.
Surplus & Trade: Extra grain (surplus) allowed river boats to trade food for timber, copper, and stone from distant mountains.
Excedente y comercio: El grano extra permitió comerciar alimentos en barco por madera, cobre y piedra de montañas lejanas.
scene.teacherPrompt: Look at the archaeological map showing how early river valley civilizations developed. We will trace the chain of causes from river flooding to long-distance trade. Listen to Leo first.

modelStudent.name: Leo
modelStudent.text: Early civilizations settled along major rivers because annual floods left nutrient-rich silt, which made the soil fertile for growing crops.

check.q: How did Leo explain the reason early people settled near rivers?

options.text: He linked annual floods to nutrient-rich silt and fertile soil using 'because' and 'which'.
He said people liked swimming in cold mountain lakes.
He listed three modern highways.

check.why: Leo chained cause and effect using 'because' and a relative clause ('which made the soil fertile').

turn1.prompt: Turn 1 (Tier A · Describe): How did farmers bring water to their fields during the dry months?
turn1.promptEs: Turno 1 (Nivel A · Describir): ¿Cómo llevaban agua los agricultores a sus campos durante los meses secos?

options: moved their cities to the desert
parts.answer: dug irrigation canals and basins

options: to channel river water to their wheat and barley fields.
to block all boats from sailing.
parts.answer: to channel river water to their wheat and barley fields.

turn1.model: During the dry months, farmers dug irrigation canals and basins to channel river water to their wheat and barley fields.

turn2.prompt: Turn 2 (Tier B · Explain Cause & Effect): How did irrigation canals lead to trade with distant mountain regions?
turn2.promptEs: Turno 2 (Nivel B · Explicar causa y efecto): ¿Cómo llevaron los canales de riego al comercio con regiones montañosas lejanas?
parts: Because irrigation allowed farmers to grow a surplus of grain,

options: cities could trade extra food by river boat
parts.answer: cities could trade extra food by river boat

options: for timber, copper, and stone from distant mountains.
parts.answer: for timber, copper, and stone from distant mountains.

turn2.model: Because irrigation allowed farmers to grow a surplus of grain, cities could trade extra food by river boat for timber, copper, and stone from distant mountains.

turn3.prompt: Turn 3 (Tier C · Extended Synthesis): Explain the two ways rivers helped ancient cities grow: both as a source of food surplus and as a transportation highway for trade.
turn3.promptEs: Turno 3 (Nivel C · Síntesis oral extendida): Explica las dos formas en que los ríos ayudaron a crecer a las ciudades antiguas: como fuente de excedente de alimentos y como vía de transporte para el comercio.
frames: Rivers supported ancient cities in two ways: first, silt and irrigation created a food surplus, and therefore ___.
Because farmers used irrigation to grow a grain surplus, merchants could use the river as a highway so ___.
turn3.model: Rivers supported ancient cities because rich silt and irrigation canals produced a grain surplus, and therefore merchants could sail along the river to trade extra food for timber and copper.

familyTalk.en: Talk at home: Why are so many major cities today still located next to rivers, bays, or ocean harbors?
familyTalk.es: Hablen en casa: ¿Por qué tantas grandes ciudades de hoy siguen estando ubicadas junto a ríos, bahías o puertos marítimos?

teacherTip.en: Model how 'surplus' bridges agriculture and economics: fertile silt -> irrigation -> food surplus -> specialization and trade.
teacherTip.es: Modele cómo 'surplus' (excedente) conecta la agricultura y la economía: limo fértil -> riego -> excedente de alimentos -> comercio.

6-8.title: Comparing Linear Plans: Initial Fee vs. Unit Rate
6-8.titleEs: Comparación de planes lineales: tarifa inicial frente a tasa unitaria

scene.heading: Community Print Shop Pricing for Club T-Shirts
scene.headingEs: Precios de la imprenta comunitaria para camisetas del club
facts: Printer A (Neighborhood Press): 0 dollar setup fee, 12 dollars per shirt. For 5 shirts = 60 dollars; for 10 shirts = 120 dollars.
Imprenta A (Prensa del Barrio): 0 dólares de cargo inicial, 12 dólares por camiseta. Por 5 = 60 dólares; por 10 = 120 dólares.
Printer B (ScreenPrint Studio): 30 dollar setup fee plus 8 dollars per shirt. For 5 shirts = 70 dollars; for 10 shirts = 110 dollars.
Imprenta B (Estudio ScreenPrint): 30 dólares de cargo inicial más 8 dólares por camiseta. Por 5 = 70 dólares; por 10 = 110 dólares.
Break-even point: At 7.5 shirts, both plans cost the same; for 8 or more shirts, Printer B costs less overall.
Punto de equilibrio: A partir de 8 camisetas o más, la Imprenta B cuesta menos en total.
scene.teacherPrompt: Look at the pricing table for Printer A and Printer B. The robotics club needs to choose which print shop to use. Listen to Maya compare the two plans.

modelStudent.name: Maya
modelStudent.text: Printer A charges 12 dollars per shirt with no setup fee, whereas Printer B charges a 30 dollar setup fee but only 8 dollars per shirt.

check.q: Why isn't one printer cheaper for every single order size?

options.text: Printer A has no setup fee for small orders, but Printer B has a lower rate per shirt for larger orders.
Both printers charge the exact same rate per shirt.
Printer B is always more expensive no matter how many shirts you buy.

check.why: Printer B starts higher because of the 30 dollar setup fee, but grows more slowly at 8 dollars per shirt.

turn1.prompt: Turn 1 (Tier A · Read the Data): If the chess club only needs 5 shirts, what does each printer charge and which one costs less?
turn1.promptEs: Turno 1 (Nivel A · Leer los datos): Si el club de ajedrez solo necesita 5 camisetas, ¿cuánto cobra cada imprenta y cuál cuesta menos?

options: 60 dollars and Printer B charges 70 dollars,
12 dollars and Printer B charges 8 dollars,
120 dollars and Printer B charges 110 dollars,
parts.answer: 60 dollars and Printer B charges 70 dollars,
Printer A costs 10 dollars less.

turn1.model: For 5 shirts, Printer A charges 60 dollars and Printer B charges 70 dollars, so Printer A costs 10 dollars less.

turn2.prompt: Turn 2 (Tier B · Explain Why): Why does Printer B become the better deal when the robotics club orders 10 shirts?
turn2.promptEs: Turno 2 (Nivel B · Explicar por qué): ¿Por qué la Imprenta B se convierte en la mejor opción cuando el club de robótica pide 10 camisetas?
parts: For 10 shirts, Printer B costs 110 dollars compared with 120 dollars at Printer A

options: because saving 4 dollars per shirt outweighs the 30 dollar setup fee.
because Printer B removes its setup fee.
since Printer A charges 30 dollars per shirt.
parts.answer: because saving 4 dollars per shirt outweighs the 30 dollar setup fee.

turn2.model: For 10 shirts, Printer B costs 110 dollars compared with 120 dollars at Printer A because saving 4 dollars per shirt outweighs the 30 dollar setup fee.

turn3.prompt: Turn 3 (Tier C · Argue with Mathematical Precision): Advise the school principal on a rule for when clubs should pick Printer A versus Printer B. Use numbers from the table, a target word, and a connector.
turn3.promptEs: Turno 3 (Nivel C · Argumentar con precisión matemática): Aconseja al director sobre cuándo los clubes deben elegir la Imprenta A frente a la Imprenta B. Usa números de la tabla, una palabra clave y un conector.
frames: If a club orders 7 shirts or fewer, they should choose Printer A because ___, whereas for 8 shirts or more ___.
Printer A is better for small orders because it has no setup fee; however, if a club orders 10 shirts, Printer B's lower rate per shirt saves 10 dollars.
turn3.model: If a club needs 5 shirts, they should choose Printer A for 60 dollars because there is no setup fee, whereas clubs ordering 8 or more shirts should pick Printer B because its 8 dollar unit rate saves money.

familyTalk.en: Talk at home: Where do we see a monthly membership fee plus a lower price per item in real life?
familyTalk.es: Hablen en casa: ¿Dónde vemos en la vida real una membresía fija más un precio más bajo por artículo?

teacherTip.en: Listen for whether students distinguish the one-time setup fee (initial value) from the cost per shirt (rate of change).
teacherTip.es: Escuche si los estudiantes distinguen entre el cargo fijo único (valor inicial) y el costo por camiseta (tasa de cambio).

6-8.title: Synthesizing Two Perspectives on School Start Times
6-8.titleEs: Síntesis de dos perspectivas sobre el horario de entrada escolar

scene.heading: Two Sources on Moving Middle School Start Time from 7:30 AM to 8:30 AM
scene.headingEs: Dos fuentes sobre cambiar la entrada de secundaria de 7:30 a. m. a 8:30 a. m.
facts: Source 1 (Pediatric Sleep Research): Adolescents experience a biological shift in melatonin, and an 8:30 AM start increases average sleep by 45 minutes and reduces tardiness.
Fuente 1 (Investigación médica del sueño): Un inicio a las 8:30 a. m. aumenta el sueño promedio en 45 minutos y reduce las llegadas tarde.
Source 2 (District Bus & Athletics Schedule): Moving start times to 8:30 AM pushes dismissal to 3:30 PM, which shortens daylight for after-school sports and shifts elementary bus routes.
Fuente 2 (Horario de autobuses y deportes): Salir a las 3:30 p. m. reduce la luz del día para los deportes y cambia las rutas de autobús.
Compromise Proposal: Flip high school and elementary bus tiers and install field lights at the middle school.
Propuesta de compromiso: Intercambiar los turnos de autobús y colocar luces en la cancha escolar.
scene.teacherPrompt: Read the summary of Source 1 and Source 2 on middle school start times. In an academic discussion, strong speakers synthesize both sources and address the trade-off. Listen to Leo.

modelStudent.name: Leo
modelStudent.text: According to Source 1, starting at 8:30 AM aligns with adolescent sleep biology and adds 45 minutes of rest, although Source 2 notes that a later dismissal affects bus routes and after-school sports.

check.q: How did Leo show he understood both sources in a single sentence?

options.text: He cited Source 1's sleep evidence and connected Source 2's scheduling concern with 'although'.
He ignored Source 2 completely and only talked about weekends.
He said both sources disagreed about everything without naming any evidence.

check.why: Using 'although' lets a speaker acknowledge a counterpoint while presenting specific evidence from both sources.

turn1.prompt: Turn 1 (Tier A · Cite Source 1): What evidence does Source 1 give in favor of an 8:30 AM start time?
turn1.promptEs: Turno 1 (Nivel A · Citar la Fuente 1): ¿Qué evidencia da la Fuente 1 a favor de entrar a las 8:30 a. m.?
parts: According to Source 1, an 8:30 AM start time

options: makes the school day 3 hours longer
parts.answer: increases average sleep by 45 minutes
reduces student tardiness.

turn1.model: According to Source 1, an 8:30 AM start time increases average sleep by 45 minutes and reduces student tardiness.

turn2.prompt: Turn 2 (Tier B · Acknowledge Counterclaim): What practical challenge from Source 2 must the school board solve?
turn2.promptEs: Turno 2 (Nivel B · Reconocer el contraargumento): ¿Qué reto práctico de la Fuente 2 debe resolver la junta escolar?

options: a 3:30 PM dismissal shortens daylight for sports
students sleep less when school starts later
parts.answer: a 3:30 PM dismissal shortens daylight for sports
requires adjusting elementary bus routes.

turn2.model: However, Source 2 points out that a 3:30 PM dismissal shortens daylight for sports and requires adjusting elementary bus routes.

turn3.prompt: Turn 3 (Tier C · Extended Argument): State your recommendation to the school board, citing evidence from Source 1 while explaining how to address Source 2's concern.
turn3.promptEs: Turno 3 (Nivel C · Argumento oral extendido): Expón tu recomendación ante la junta escolar, citando evidencia de la Fuente 1 y explicando cómo resolver la preocupación de la Fuente 2.
frames: Although a later dismissal affects bus routes and sports schedules, the board should adopt the 8:30 AM start because ___.
The district should move start times to 8:30 AM because students gain 45 minutes of sleep; however, they should also ___.
turn3.model: Although a later schedule requires adjusting bus routes, the board should adopt the 8:30 AM start because students gain 45 minutes of sleep and reduce tardiness.

familyTalk.en: Talk at home: What morning routine helps everyone in our home feel rested and ready for the day?
familyTalk.es: Hablen en casa: ¿Qué rutina matutina ayuda a que todos en casa se sientan descansados y listos para el día?

teacherTip.en: Point out how 'According to Source 1...' + 'Although Source 2 notes...' gives students a portable template for any WIDA synthesis task.
teacherTip.es: Señale cómo 'According to Source 1...' + 'Although Source 2 notes...' ofrece a los estudiantes una estructura portátil para cualquier tarea de síntesis.
